_: Every rule id the check engine can register, resolved THE WAY THE ENGINE RESOLVES THEM, so a
lesson's guard can be checked against the full set rather than against the port's progress.
WHY THIS IS DATA: mistakes.guard_covered checks that a block-severity lesson names a guard rule
that EXISTS. My first implementation resolved against ruleinventory::all_ids() - the rules the
PORT has implemented - while the rule must resolve against the rules the ENGINE registers. A
lesson guarding on a rule that exists and is enforced was reported as 'not a rule this engine
registers': Rust said 4, Python said 0. A guard check against an incomplete port is NOT A WEAKER
CHECK, IT IS A WRONG ONE - it would tell authors to delete guards on real rules, and it would
stop being wrong only when the port finished, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHEN THE CHECK STOPS MATTERING.
WHY IT HAS 53 IDS AND NOT 40: the engine resolves guards from THREE sources, not one -
checkrules.rules() (40), each module's own register_rules() (13 more), and prlint.GATE_RULES,
which are the gates raised against a PR body rather than against repo state. My first data file
took only checkrules.rules(), so the four lessons whose guards name a prlint gate were reported
as unregistered - the SAME false positive in a new place.
The lesson repeats: I asked 'what rules are registered' and answered with the first list I found,
twice, instead of reading the function that answers the question. This file is that function's
Refresh it when a rule is added or removed. The test asserts the count so a drift is a failing
test rather than a silently wrong answer.
